creator: bengusberg
title: Four-persona 'board of advisors' in Claude Cowork (Operator, Investor, Customer, Skeptic) that debates a decision and votes

tools.name: Claude Cowork
tools.detail: Prompts typed into Cowork tab; model selector shows 'Sonnet 5 · High'

claims: Creator is a Stanford founder of an AI startup that has raised $4 million
Uses four Claude agents as a board of advisors; 'saves me a lot of mental back-and-forth'
You remain CEO and can take or ignore the board's advice
how_to_steps: Open Claude Cowork and prompt: 'Create a board of advisors with 4 agents. Each with specific personas' — Agent 1 Elite Operator (practical, says what breaks); Agent 2 Investor (strategy, does it make money); Agent 3 Customer (does anyone want this); Agent 4 Skeptic (only job is to say no and explain why)
Bring a business decision and prompt: 'Should I double my prices? Ask my board of advisors. Have them debate in front of me and cast a vote.'
Decide yourself whether to follow the vote
on_screen_only: Cowork prompt box text: 'Create a board of advisors with 4 agents. Each with specific personas'
Second prompt: 'Should I double my prices? Ask my board of advisors. Have them debate in front of me and cast a vote.'
UI chrome: Chat | Cowork, 'Project or folder', 'Manual', model 'Sonnet 5 · High', '2+ more usage until August 5'
Four colored robot icons (yellow, purple, green, blue) for the four personas

relevance.why: A structured devil's-advocate pass on pricing/product decisions is useful for a solo founder with no cofounder, and the exact prompts are shown; overlaps with a council-style review already in use.

implement_score.why: Ten minutes to save the two prompts as a Claude Code skill or Cowork preset; the Skeptic persona is the valuable part. Cheap enough to just do.

verify: Does Cowork persist the four personas across sessions or must they be re-created each time (a saved skill/prompt file would solve this)?
Any evidence persona debate improves decision quality vs one well-prompted critique?
